title: Phone Speaker Cleaner: Safe Ways to Clean
meta_description: CleanKoach cannot clean a phone speaker, because it is software. Here is how to clean muffled speakers gently, and what to avoid, without damaging the phone.
tagline: CleanKoach cleans storage, not speakers. Here is the gentle way
quick_answer: No app can clean a phone speaker, and CleanKoach does not claim to. A muffled speaker is usually blocked by dust or lint. Turn the phone off, wipe the grille with a dry soft cloth, use a soft dry brush gently, keep moisture out of the openings and avoid compressed air.
intro: If calls sound faint or music is muffled, first rule out a software cause, then look at the speaker grille. Here is a cautious order of steps.

sections.html: Sound is made by a physical part. CleanKoach frees storage space. It does not affect the speaker, and a "speaker cleaner" app cannot remove dust. Some apps play tones and claim to clear water, but cleaning the grille by hand is what removes dust.
see: Best phone cleaner app for Android

sections.h2: Rule out the easy causes first
sections.html:
1. Check volume and mode. Silent mode, a low volume slider or Do Not Disturb can look like a fault.
  2. Check Bluetooth. Audio may be going to an earbud or speaker you forgot.
  3. Remove the case. Some cases cover or partly block the speaker.
  4. Restart the phone.

1. Turn the phone off and unplug cables.
  2. Wipe the surface with a soft, lint-free cloth. Use a dry one for dust.
  3. Brush gently. A clean, soft, dry brush, such as an unused soft toothbrush, loosens dust. Brush lightly across the grille.
  4. Turn the phone grille-side down and tap it lightly against your hand to shake out loose dust.
  5. Test the sound with a song or a call.

• Liquids in openings: Apple and Google both say to keep moisture and soap out of openings.
  • Compressed air: Apple says not to use it on iPhone and Google advises against it on Pixel.
  • Sharp tools: a pin can tear the speaker mesh.
  • Hard pressing: the mesh is thin.

sections.html: If the sound is still faint or distorted after cleaning, or the phone has been in liquid, ask the maker or a repair shop. Do not open the phone yourself.

faqs.q: Can an app clean my phone speaker?
faqs.a: No. A speaker is hardware. CleanKoach frees storage space and cannot clean speakers.

faqs.q: Why is my phone speaker muffled?
faqs.a: Often dust or lint over the grille, a case that blocks it, or a volume or audio setting. Check settings and the case first.

faqs.q: How do I clean a phone speaker safely?
faqs.a: Turn the phone off, wipe with a soft dry cloth, brush the grille gently with a soft dry brush and shake out loose dust.

faqs.q: Can I use compressed air on a speaker?
faqs.a: Apple says not to use it on iPhone and Google advises against it on Pixel, so avoid it.

faqs.q: Can I use liquid or alcohol on the grille?
faqs.a: Keep liquids out of openings. Apple and Google both advise keeping moisture out.

faqs.q: Do speaker cleaner apps that play sound work?
faqs.a: They cannot remove dust. Cleaning the grille by hand is what removes it.

faqs.q: Is a toothbrush safe for the speaker?
faqs.a: A clean, soft, dry brush used lightly is gentler than a pin. Do not press hard.

faqs.q: What if the speaker still sounds bad after cleaning?
faqs.a: Ask the maker or a repair shop. It may be a damaged speaker.
No. CleanKoach does not change audio settings or hardware.
